boilerplate.section_intro: This section consists of questions and problems involving quantitative reasoning.  Each question is followed by four possible responses.  Choose the correct answer and mark its number in the appropriate place on the answer sheet.

boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro:
Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow.

A certain farmer has a square field in which vegetables are grown.  The field is divided into 11 rectangular plots, as described in the graph.
Each rectangle in the graph describes a plot, and written in it are the name of the vegetable and the price (in shekels) at which the farmer sells one kg of this vegetable.  The fill of the rectangle represents the ripening season of the vegetable (see key).  Empty rectangles represent empty plots, in which the farmer has not planted anything.
Marking posts are located along the entire perimeter of the field.  The distance between every two adjacent posts is 5 metres.

For example: In one of the plots the farmer grows tomatoes, which he sells at 6 shekels per kg.  The width of this plot is 15 metres, and the tomatoes in it ripen in the summer.

Study the graph below, then answer the five questions that follow. The graph describes the apartment market in a certain country in the years 2000-2009. The graph presents the number of apartments that were sold in each year and three measures relating to their prices: – The average price of all the apartments that were sold in that year. – The average price of the cheap apartments that were sold. The cheap apartments (25% of all the apartments that were sold) are those that were sold at the lowest prices in that year. – The average price of the expensive apartments that were sold. The expensive apartments (25% of all the apartments that were sold) are those that were sold at the highest prices in that year. The number of apartments that were sold in each year is marked in the graph by bold points connected by a dotted line (in relation to the right-hand axis). The three price measures are marked on the vertical segments (in relation to the left-hand axis, see key). Note: Assume that no apartment was sold more than once during the period described in the graph. For example: In 2000, 40,000 apartments were sold. Their average price was $175,000. Of these, the 10,000 cheapest apartments were sold at an average price of $125,000 and the 10,000 most expensive apartments were sold at an average price of $250,000.

What is the difference between the largest two-digit number whose tens digit is 2 times as much as its units digit, and the smallest two-digit number that satisfies this condition?

methods.text: Tens \(= 2 \times\) units, so the number is \(\overline{(2u)u}\) with \(2u \le 9\). That gives \(u \in \{1,2,3,4\}\) and the numbers 21, 42, 63, 84.
Largest minus smallest is \(84 - 21 = 63\). The constraint caps \(u\) at 4, which is what makes the list so short.

questions.stem:
Moti and Smadar are picking grapefruits in an orchard.
Moti picks at a rate of 3 grapefruits in 10 minutes.
Smadar picks at a rate of 5 grapefruits in 15 minutes.

How many grapefruits do they pick together in two hours?

methods.text: Moti picks \(\frac{3}{10}\) a minute and Smadar \(\frac13\), so \(\frac{19}{30}\) together. Over 120 minutes that is 76.
Both rates are given per different windows, so convert both to per-minute before adding — the ground rule of the whole topic.

questions.stem:
Given:  x + 2y = 5
2x + y = 13

x + y = ?

methods.text: Add the two equations: \(3x + 3y = 18\), so \(x + y = 6\). Neither letter needs to be found.
Solving properly gives \(x = 7\) and \(y = -1\), whose sum is 6 — the same answer through more work.

questions.stem: Tal wore on each one of the 7 days of the week a different combination of a sweater with a scarf. Tal has three different sweaters. How many scarves does Tal have at least?

In the accompanying figure ABCD is a square.

AE = BH = 5 cm

What is the size of the dark area (in cm²)?

Five card players are sitting in a circle (see figure). Player A divides among them a deck of 104 cards in the following manner: He gives the first pair of cards to himself, the next pair of cards he gives to player B, and so he continues clockwise. Which player will receive the last pair of cards?

methods.text: 104 cards dealt in pairs is 52 deals, cycling through 5 players. So the question is \(52 \bmod 5\).
\(52 = 10 \times 5 + 2\), so after ten full cycles two more deals happen: A then B. The last pair goes to B.

questions.stem:
Given:  x·y < |x·y| < y

According to this information, which of the following statements is necessarily true?

methods.text: Each link does one job. \(xy<|xy|\) can only happen when \(xy\) is negative. \(|xy|<y\) needs \(y\) positive, since an absolute value is never negative. Negative product with positive \(y\) makes \(x\) negative. Finally \(|x|\,y<y\), and dividing by the positive \(y\) gives \(|x|<1\).

Read the chain as three separate facts rather than one object: the first fixes the sign of the product, the second the sign of \(y\), the third the size of \(x\). Together they place \(x\) between \(-1\) and 0.

A plot is considered more "expensive" the higher the ratio  \(\frac{\text{price per kg (in shekels)}}{\text{plot area (in m²)}}\)  is.

Which of the following plots is the most expensive?

The farmer has a rectangular plastic sheet that protects the vegetables that ripen in winter from hail. The dimensions of the sheet are (40 metres) × (30 metres), and it is impossible to divide it. The farmer covered with this sheet the maximum possible area of the plots of vegetables that ripen in winter. What is the area of the plots of vegetables that ripen in winter (in m²) that is not covered by the sheet?
\(a \cdot \left(\frac{a}{4} + b + \frac{b^2}{a}\right) = ?\)  ,  \((a \neq 0)\)

methods.text: Multiplying through gives \(\frac{a^2}{4} + ab + b^2\). The outer terms are \(\left(\frac a2\right)^2\) and \(b^2\), and twice their product is \(ab\) — so it is \(\left(\frac a2 + b\right)^2\).
Take \(a=2, b=1\): the expression is \(2\left(\frac12+1+\frac12\right) = 4\), and option (1) gives \((1+1)^2 = 4\).

questions.stem: During a certain week the price of 1 kg of cherries underwent the following changes: On the second day the price of 1 kg of cherries was 75% of its price on the first day. From the third day onwards the price rose each day by 20% in relation to the price on the previous day. On which day was the price of 1 kg of cherries for the first time more than 10% higher than its price on the first day?

methods.text: Track the multiplier from day one: 1, then 0.75, then 0.9, then 1.08, then 1.296. The first value above \(1.10\) is the fifth day — Thursday.
Wednesday is up 8%, which clears the first day's price but not the 10% the question demands. Reading the threshold precisely is what separates the two middle options.

questions.stem:
Tamar travels a certain distance in a certain time.  Oded travels a distance that is 2 times shorter in a time that is 3 times longer.  Each of them has a fixed speed.

Oded's speed is ______ Tamar's speed.

methods.text: Oded's speed is \(\frac{d/2}{3t} = \frac{d}{6t}\), which is one sixth of Tamar's \(\frac dt\).
Tamar: 6 km in 1 hour, so 6 km/h. Oded: 3 km in 3 hours, so 1 km/h. Six times smaller. Picking numbers that make both halvings and thirdings whole takes three seconds.
Half the distance and triple the time both slow him down, so the factors multiply rather than partly cancel — which is why \(\frac32\) is offered as a trap.

questions.stem: The positive whole number x is called a "common divisor" of the positive whole numbers a and b if both a and also b are divisible by x without a remainder. Which of the following numbers is not a common divisor of 84 and 210?

methods.text: A common divisor of both must divide their \(\gcd\). \(84 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 7\) and \(210 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7\), so \(\gcd = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 7 = 42\).
\(7\), \(6\) and \(3\) all divide 42; \(4\) does not, because 210 has only one factor of 2. Checking against 210 alone is the fastest route — it is odd-ish in its 2s.

questions.stem:
A certain flower had 10 milligrams (mg) of nectar.  At a certain moment a bee arrived at the flower, a minute after it a second bee joined it, a minute later a third bee joined them, and so on.  Each bee sucks nectar from the flower at a fixed rate of 1 mg per minute, until the nectar in the flower ran out.

How many mg of nectar altogether did the first bee that arrived at the flower suck?

methods.text: Bees accumulate: minute 1 has one bee taking 1 mg, minute 2 has two taking 2, and so on. The running total is \(1, 3, 6, 10\).
The 10 mg is gone during the fourth minute. Triangular numbers rather than a constant rate — the workforce grows every minute.

questions.stem: a and b are consecutive whole numbers, 1 < a < b. (2a–b) is necessarily –

methods.text: Consecutive with \(a < b\) means \(b = a+1\), so \(2a - b = 2a - a - 1 = a - 1\). That is one less than \(a\), so it is necessarily smaller than \(a\).
Its parity is not fixed — \(a=2\) gives 1, odd; \(a=3\) gives 2, even — which kills both parity options at once.

questions.stem: A, B, C and D are consecutive digits among the digits 1 to 9, with A < B < C < D. The sum of the two two-digit numbers AB and CD is a two-digit number. How many possible values does A have?

methods.text: Consecutive digits mean \(B = A+1\), \(C = A+2\), \(D = A+3\). Then \(\overline{AB} + \overline{CD} = (10A + A + 1) + (10A + 20 + A + 3) = 22A + 24\).
For that to stay a two-digit number, \(22A + 24 \le 99\), so \(A \le 3\). And \(A \ge 1\), with \(D = A+3 \le 9\) allowing up to 6. So \(A \in \{1,2,3\}\) — three values.

questions.stem: In a certain game, on each turn a player can lose one point or gain a fixed whole number of points P (at the start of the game the score is 0, and a negative score during the game is also possible). Danny played eight turns in the game, and at the end he had 28 points. It is known that he gained in more than half of the turns. P = ?
A cylinder is given whose height is 3 cm and whose lateral surface area is 6 cm². What is the volume of the cylinder (in cm³)?

x is greater than y by 20%.

y equals ______ percent of x.

methods.text: Set \(y = 100\), so \(x = 120\). Then \(y\) as a percentage of \(x\) is \(\frac{100}{120} = 83\frac13\%\).
Not \(80\%\). Reversing a percentage relationship means taking a reciprocal, not subtracting from 100 — the single most common percentage error there is.
